    <descript>
      <abstract>This tile of the 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) seamless products is 1 Arc Second resolution.  3DEP data serve as the elevation layer of The National Map, and provide basic elevation information for Earth science studies and mapping applications in the United States. Scientists and resource managers use 3DEP data for global change research, hydrologic modeling, resource monitoring, mapping and visualization, and many other applications. 3DEP data compose an elevation dataset that consists of seamless layers and a high resolution layer.  Each of these layers consists of the best available raster elevation data of the conterminous United States, Alaska, Hawaii, territorial islands, Mexico and Canada.  3DEP data are updated continually as new data become available. Seamless 3DEP data are derived from diverse source data that are processed to a common coordinate system and unit of vertical measure. These data are distributed in geographic coordinates in units of decimal degrees, and in conformance with the North American Datum of 1983 (NAD 83). All elevation values are in meters and, over the conterminous United States, are referenced to the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD 88). The vertical reference will vary in other areas. Seamless 3DEP data are available nationally (except for Alaska) at resolutions of 1 arc-second (approximately 30 meters) and 1/3 arc-second (approximately 10 meters). In most of Alaska, only lower resolution source data are available. As a result, most seamless 3DEP data for Alaska are at 2 arc-second (approximately 60 meters) grid spacing. Part of Alaska is available at the 1 and 1/3 arc-second resolutions from interferometric synthetic aperture radar (ifsar) collections starting in 2010.  Plans are in place for collection of statewide ifsar in Alaska. All 3DEP products are public domain.</abstract>
      <purpose>The 3DEP data serves as the elevation layer of The National Map, and provides basic elevation information for Earth science studies and mapping applications in the United States.  The data are utilized by the scientific and resource management communities for global change research, hydrologic modeling, resource monitoring, mapping and visualization applications.</purpose>
      <supplinf>This tile of seamless 3DEP dataset is 1 Arc Second resolution,  TIFF file format, and covers a 1 degree block. Data may be downloaded through The National Map Viewer: https://nationalmap.gov/viewer.html.  Direct links for direct access by automated services are provided in the "Distribution" section of this metadata.</supplinf>

    <descript>
      <abstract>This tile of the 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) seamless products is 1 Arc Second resolution.  3DEP data serve as the elevation layer of The National Map, and provide basic elevation information for Earth science studies and mapping applications in the United States. Scientists and resource managers use 3DEP data for global change research, hydrologic modeling, resource monitoring, mapping and visualization, and many other applications. 3DEP data compose an elevation dataset that consists of seamless layers and a high resolution layer.  Each of these layers consists of the best available raster elevation data of the conterminous United States, Alaska, Hawaii, territorial islands, Mexico and Canada.  3DEP data are updated continually as new data become available. Seamless 3DEP data are derived from diverse source data that are processed to a common coordinate system and unit of vertical measure. These data are distributed in geographic coordinates in units of decimal degrees, and in conformance with the North American Datum of 1983 (NAD 83). All elevation values are in meters and, over the conterminous United States, are referenced to the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD 88). The vertical reference will vary in other areas. Seamless 3DEP data are available nationally (except for Alaska) at resolutions of 1 arc-second (approximately 30 meters) and 1/3 arc-second (approximately 10 meters). In most of Alaska, only lower resolution source data are available. As a result, most seamless 3DEP data for Alaska are at 2 arc-second (approximately 60 meters) grid spacing. Part of Alaska is available at the 1 and 1/3 arc-second resolutions from interferometric synthetic aperture radar (ifsar) collections starting in 2010.  Plans are in place for collection of statewide ifsar in Alaska. All 3DEP products are public domain.</abstract>
      <purpose>The 3DEP data serves as the elevation layer of The National Map, and provides basic elevation information for Earth science studies and mapping applications in the United States.  The data are utilized by the scientific and resource management communities for global change research, hydrologic modeling, resource monitoring, mapping and visualization applications.</purpose>

    <descript>
      <abstract>This tile of the 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) seamless products is 1 Arc Second resolution.  3DEP data serve as the elevation layer of The National Map, and provide basic elevation information for Earth science studies and mapping applications in the United States. Scientists and resource managers use 3DEP data for global change research, hydrologic modeling, resource monitoring, mapping and visualization, and many other applications. 3DEP data compose an elevation dataset that consists of seamless layers and a high resolution layer. Seamless 3DEP data are derived from diverse source data that are processed to a common coordinate system and unit of vertical measure. These data are distributed in geographic coordinates in units of decimal degrees, and in conformance with the North American Datum of 1983 (NAD 83). Seamless 3DEP data are available nationally (except for Alaska) at resolutions of 1 arc-second (approximately 30 meters) and 1/3 arc-second (approximately 10 meters). In most of Alaska, only lower resolution source data are available. As a result, most seamless 3DEP data for Alaska are at 2 arc-second (approximately 60 meters) grid spacing. Part of Alaska is available at the 1 and 1/3 arc-second resolutions from interferometric synthetic aperture radar (ifsar) collections starting in 2010.  Plans are in place for collection of statewide ifsar in Alaska. All 3DEP products are public domain.</abstract>

# Upper Savannah original terrain intake

This source packet resolves the original 217-HUC model domain and its 1000 m buffer
to nine original USGS 3DEP one arc-second products. It retains all nine publisher
directory bodies and all nine original FGDC XML files, with exact bytes and SHA256.
The complete inventory is inventory.json in this directory.

## Original geographic selection

The original 5062-byte EPSG:5070 source plan has SHA256
41296472d82dfb53e65b9fa86045cf5facba33d567977269f69437d53f9eefa9.
Its buffered_domain_bounds are the input to the retained derivation. The Albers
inverse uses the NAD83 GRS80 ellipsoid, latitude origin 23°, central meridian −96°,
and standard parallels 29.5° and 45.5°. Across this positive-easting rectangle below
rho0, longitude increases with x and y; latitude decreases with x and increases
with y. Its corner values therefore give exact extrema of the transformed rectangle.
The inverse uses the EPSG Albers q equation with a converged latitude solve.

The resulting NAD83 geographic envelope is
[-83.8743318014598,33.335571299652926,-81.48972373077227,35.25542325044666].
The coarse acquisition envelope is rounded outward with at least 0.01 degree padding:
[-83.89,33.32,-81.47,35.27]. This padding leaves the same nine one-degree tile IDs
and accommodates the coarse geographic source-index selection. The original
model grid and domain mask stay with the native Workspace.

## Continue in the existing application

Use the accepting application's existing GIS Python, actual retained terrain
store and original Workspace. Run the existing maintained commands from the
application directory. The terrain store belongs on the receiving operation's
actual retained filesystem. Acquisition keeps original source entities and their
own recovery records; reusing that store resumes the same transfers.

```sh
"$GIS_PYTHON" -B -m source_tools.terrain_cli --store "$TERRAIN_STORE" discover \
  --bounds -83.89 33.32 -81.47 35.27 \
  --title "Upper Savannah retained 3DEP source edition"
```

Use the actual relative catalog_path returned by discover, joined to the terrain
store. The existing acquire API resolves that full path under the same store:

```sh
"$GIS_PYTHON" -B -m source_tools.terrain_cli --store "$TERRAIN_STORE" acquire \
  "$TERRAIN_STORE/$CATALOG_RELATIVE_PATH" --workers 2
```

The maintained discovery operation captures current original HTTP bodies and
provider headers into its own upstate.terrain-catalog/v1 record. This packet's
original bodies and listed editions let the receiver compare the same selected
publisher products. Keep the acquired XML hashes beside this inventory; if a
mutable USGS current product changes, retain its actual new edition through the
same native catalog/source machinery.

Once the original numeric NLCD source and original domain are imported, bind
these nine terrain sources to that exact grid through the existing Workspace:

```sh
"$GIS_PYTHON" -B -m source_tools.terrain_cli --store "$TERRAIN_STORE" plan-workspace \
  --workspace "$NATIVE_WORKSPACE" \
  --reference-collection-id "$NLCD_COLLECTION_ID" --reference-source-id "$NLCD_SOURCE_ID" \
  --domain-collection-id "$DOMAIN_COLLECTION_ID" --domain-source-id "$DOMAIN_SOURCE_ID" \
  --buffer-m 1000 --resampling bilinear --chunk-size 1024
```

Select the exact nine source IDs returned by acquire using repeated --source-id
arguments if the existing store already contains another terrain edition. Read
the returned plan_id, then finish and import it into the same Workspace:

```sh
"$GIS_PYTHON" -B -m source_tools.terrain_cli --store "$TERRAIN_STORE" prepare \
  "$TERRAIN_PLAN_ID" --workspace "$NATIVE_WORKSPACE" --progress
```

The maintained preparation builds a source-lattice mosaic and performs the
selected reprojection onto the original NLCD grid. Its original inspector,
completed manifest, source entry and workspace source ID are the receiving result
for regional_job.run_core. Keep those actual returned paths/IDs in the original
regional source operation alongside the NLCD/PRISM/soil inputs.
